Title: Cops probing claims Hadi was offered US backing to topple BN govt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are investigating claims that PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang was offered cooperation by the United States to topple the Barisan Nasional (BN) government in 2014.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar S Muthuvelu said 12 police reports had been lodged over the matter, while statements had been recorded from 12 witnesses.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
"Investigation under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code involves an offence relating to statements that could cause public alarm and, upon conviction, carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine, or both.
"Investigation under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 involves the improper use of network facilities or network services. Upon conviction, the offence carries a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment for up to two years, or both," he said in a statement tonight.
M Kumar said Hadi's statement would be recorded in the near future to facilitate the completion of the investigation.
He also advised the public against making speculation that could interfere with the investigation process, and urged them to use social media responsibly and refrain from making statements that could affect public order and safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 4-month-old baby dies after being found unconscious at nursery
Article:
DUNGUN: A four-month-old baby girl died after she was found unconscious at a nursery in Bandar Al Muktafi Billah Shah here yesterday.
Dungun district police chief Superintendent Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said the baby was pronounced dead at Dungun Hospital at about 12.45pm.
He said police received a report on the incident at 3.41pm.
"The baby was sent to the nursery by her mother at about 8am in good health.
"However, at about 10am, nursery staff found her unconscious and sent her to Durian Mas Health Clinic before she was referred to Dungun Hospital," he said.
Nik Ab Halim said medical officers at the hospital examined the baby and attempted to revive her by providing respiratory assistance.
"However, she was pronounced dead at about 12.45pm.
"Initial examination found no physical injuries on the victim's body. A post-mortem will be conducted to determine the cause of death," he said.
He said police had opened an investigation under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001.
"We will conduct a detailed investigation to determine whether there was any element of negligence or neglect while the victim was under the care of the nursery.
"The two caregivers on duty at the time have been identified and will have their statements recorded to assist the investigation," he said.
He added that police would also record statements from the parents and relevant witnesses, besides obtaining medical reports and opinions from the medical authorities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia, Thailand to step up coordination on border security, smuggling
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Thailand will streamline coordination among agencies from both countries, particularly on security and development in border areas, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan.
He said the matter was among the issues discussed during his meeting with Thailand's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow today, with both sides seeking to better coordinate existing cooperation, including efforts to combat smuggling.
He said better coordination was important to prevent duplication of efforts by agencies from both countries, which could result in a waste of resources, while ensuring that the shared vision of both countries' leaders to strengthen bilateral ties could be effectively realised.
"We want to streamline coordination to ensure that, particularly in terms of border security, we no longer face smuggling issues that cause losses to both sides.
"Both Malaysia and Thailand suffer losses, as goods are smuggled into Thailand, just as goods are smuggled from Thailand into Malaysia," he told a press conference after hosting a luncheon for his Thai counterpart in conjunction with Sihasak's two-day working visit to Malaysia.
Mohamad said both sides also discussed a proposal to coordinate the construction of border fencing, with Thailand planning to build fences in areas that have yet to be fenced by Malaysia to avoid duplication.
"Where we have already built a fence, they (Thailand) will not build one. Instead, they will construct fences in areas that currently lack them. This represents cooperation in terms of both security and border management," he said.
On the situation in southern Thailand, Mohamad said Malaysia, which has been entrusted with facilitating the peace dialogue process, would continue to assist efforts to advance negotiations towards a more positive outcome.
He said this was important as the long-running negotiation process had yet to achieve the desired progress.
"This effort is vital to ensure Malaysia can contribute as a facilitator, helping to transform the region into a peaceful area and a zone for joint Malaysia-Thailand border development," he said.
He added that both countries were also cooperating to address flooding along the Golok River and in Rantau Panjang, including through river deepening projects and the construction of flood barriers.
Mohamad said Malaysia, through the Energy Transition and Water Transformation Ministry (Petra), had secured Thailand's agreement to carry out dredging works along the Golok River, extending to its estuary, to ensure unobstructed water flow during periods of heavy rainfall.

Title: Thunderstorm, heavy rain warning issued for six states until 1am
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several areas in six states until 1am today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia said the states involved are Kedah, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Sarawak and Sabah.
In Kedah, the affected areas are Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu, while in Perak, they are Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Larut Matang and Selama.
The same warning has also been issued for Kuala Krai in Kelantan; Besut in Terengganu; and Sri Aman (Lingga, Sri Aman and Lubok Antu), Betong (Betong), Mukah (Daro and Matu) and Kapit (Song and Bukit Mabong) in Sarawak.
In Sabah, the affected areas are Sandakan (Telupid, Paitan, Kinabatangan, Labuk and Sugut and Tongod), Tawau (Lahad Datu), Pantai Barat (Ranau) and Pedalaman (Pensiangan).

Title: Freedom of Information Bill committee to hold National Townhall on Sept 28
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Parliamentary Special Select Committee on the Freedom of Information Bill 2026 will hold a National Townhall on Sept 28 to facilitate wider stakeholder and public participation in scrutinising the proposed legislation.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said said the committee agreed to hold the session after considering views and feedback from stakeholders.
She said the townhall would help ensure key issues concerning the Bill's framework were thoroughly considered before the committee finalised its recommendations and views.
The committee had also heard views and presentations from Emeritus Professor Datuk Dr Shad Saleem Faruqi on constitutional and legal perspectives, as well as additional feedback from the Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) on issues raised during previous meetings.
"This is among the important reforms that require in-depth and balanced scrutiny to ensure that the framework established can be implemented effectively and responsibly, taking into account the public interest as well as relevant legal considerations," she said in a statement after chairing the committee's meeting today.
Azalina also chaired the Third Meeting of the Parliamentary Special Select Committee on the Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill 2026.
The committee examined AGC feedback on views from various stakeholders, including Federal Court judge Tan Sri Nallini Pathmanathan and the Malaysian Bar Council.
It also examined the outcome of discussions between the Legal Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Department, the Transport Ministry, AGC and the Office of the Chief Registrar of the Federal Court to reach a consensus on several issues raised before the committee's report is finalised.
Azalina said the meeting on the Admiralty Jurisdiction Bill was attended by the MPs for Tebrau, Simpang Renggam, Stampin, Lumut, Padang Rengas and Jerantut.
The Freedom of Information Bill committee meeting involved the MPs for Selayang, Kuala Pilah, Bangi, Puchong, Lubok Antu, Kota Belud and Pasir Mas.

Title: 59 KLIA flights cancelled as Indonesia closes airspace over volcanic eruption
Article:
SEPANG: A total of 59 flights at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 and Terminal 2 were cancelled following the closure of Indonesian airspace due to a volcanic eruption.
Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (MAHB) senior general manager Hasman Abd Muhimim said 6,279 passengers were affected by the cancellations.
He said almost all affected passengers had been assisted, either with hotel accommodation in the Klang Valley or alternative travel arrangements to destinations in Indonesia.
"Of that number, only 56 passengers are still at KLIA, and we continue to assist them so they can remain comfortable at the airport and receive attention from the airlines, ground handlers and airport operator," he said.
On flights scheduled for tomorrow, Hasman said MAHB had so far only received notifications of cancellations for today.
He said the situation would depend on developments regarding the airspace closure announced by the Indonesian aviation authorities.
"So far, the closure is only until 7pm today, and we are waiting for further notification on whether it will be extended into tomorrow.
"Passengers scheduled to fly tomorrow should contact their respective airlines for the latest information and to determine their next flight arrangements," he said.
Meanwhile, affected passenger Fintje Wondal said she and several family members had decided to wait for a replacement flight after their flight to Jakarta was cancelled.
"We are still postponing our flight until tomorrow. We will take a replacement flight tomorrow because we were told there were no flights today," she said.
Another passenger, Raya Sesan Firdaus, said she was still waiting for confirmation on whether her flight to Indonesia could proceed.
She said her group was in Malaysia for an educational tour after first visiting Singapore.
"My mother is a little worried, but I have reassured her that everything is fine here.
"The service here has been very good. The airport is also fine, everything is smooth and safe," she said.

Title: Fitch downgrades Genting ratings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Fitch Ratings has lowered its credit rating on Genting Bhd and its two subsidiaries, citing expectations that the group's debt burden will remain high in the next three years.
The ratings agency expects Genting's net debt to stay above four times its earnings during the period.
"We expect the pace of deleveraging to be slow due to substantial capex to expand key properties, including those in Singapore and New York.
"This is compounded by a slower-than-expected earnings ramp-up at Genting New York LLC because of high start-up operating costs, as well as a more gradual recovery across Genting's other gaming operations," it said.
The agency has downgraded Genting to BBB- from BBB, Genting Overseas Holdings Ltd's was downgraded to BBB- from BBB while Resorts World Las Vegas LLC now sits one notch lower at BB+.
Genting New York's capex will likely remain high at an average of about US$800 million per year over the medium term.
"We expect Genting New York's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (ebitda) to increase to US$208 million in 2026 as the casino ramps up.
"This is slightly lower than our previous expectation of US$215 million due to high start-up operating costs.
"Our forecast assumes that by 2028, ebitda from Genting New York will reach around US$450 million as more tables and slot machines are added, while ebitda margin improves as costs normalise," it added.
Gaming revenue in Singapore is also expected to be flat this year due to renovation at its hotels and casino.
"We expect muted revenue growth for the Malaysian properties, amid high travel costs and macroeconomic uncertainties," it said.

Title: Taska worker remanded 6 days over alleged rough treatment of 2-year-old
Article:
TEMERLOH: A 25-year-old female childcare worker has been remanded for six days to assist investigations into the alleged rough treatment of a 2-year-old girl at a nursery in Mentakab here.
Temerloh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the woman was detained following a police report lodged by the girl's 29-year-old mother on Sept 5.
The remand order, effective today until Sept 12, was issued by Temerloh magistrate Anis Adlina Abu Johan.
Nasyim said police received the report about 6pm after the mother claimed her daughter had been subjected to rough treatment by a caregiver while at the nursery.
The case came to light after a recording related to the incident went viral on social media on Friday.
Police had earlier detected a social media post about the alleged incident before the girl's mother lodged a formal report.
The case is being investigated under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years, a fine of up to RM50,000, or both upon conviction.
Nasyim had previously said police were conducting further investigations and would refer the investigation papers to the public prosecutor for further instructions.
Police are continuing their investigations.

Title: MNHB unit in JV with Pembinaan Tajri for RM67mil TNB cable installation contract
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: MN Holdings Bhd's (MNHB) wholly owned unit, MN Utilities Engineering Sdn Bhd (MNUE) and Pembinaan Tajri Sdn Bhd  (PTSB) has bagged a contract for the installation of a new 275 kilovolt (kV) cable from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB).
The contract, worth RM67.31 million, was secured via an unincorporated joint-venture (JV) arrangement between MNUE and PTSB.
In a filing to Bursa Malaysia today, MNHB said MNUE and PTSB received the contract award for the installation of new 275 kV reconfiguration underground cable from LILO Point to Intel Electronic Malaysia switching station for 275kV bulk supply to Intel Penang from TNB.
"Both MNUE and PTSB have agreed to collaborate and work together via an unincorporated JV for the contract," it added.
Works will be in the proportion of 80 per cent (MNUE) and 20 per cent (PTSB) or such percentage proportion that is to be mutually agreed upon by both companies.
The contract shall be effective from Sept 4, 2026, with a completion period of 540 days from the commencement date.
The parties will be required to furnish a performance security worth RM3.36 million being five per cent of the accepted contract amount within 56 days from Sept 4.

Title: Leapmotor EVs go local
Article:
STELLANTIS Malaysia has begun local assembly of the Leapmotor C10 and B10 electric SUVs at its Stellantis Gurun plant in Kedah, marking a new step in the group's push to expand EV manufacturing in the country.
The locally assembled models will be available through authorised Leapmotor dealers nationwide.
Stellantis has invested 5.3 million euros to develop local production capabilities, including upgrades to the production line and plant infrastructure.
The company said Leapmotor and Stellantis operate under a unified global compliance framework to maintain consistent manufacturing standards across locally assembled vehicles.
The locally assembled C10 is offered with two new exterior colours — Violet and Lightning White — alongside Canopy Grey and Glazed Green.
The SUV is powered by a 69.9kWh battery and a permanent magnet synchronous motor producing 218hp and 320Nm.
It offers a driving range of up to 424km on a full charge under the WLTP standard.
The C10 also features OEKO-TEX Standard 100-certified, baby-friendly silicone textile upholstery.
The Glazed Green variant comes with a Camel Brown interior, while other exterior colours are paired with a Black cabin.
The B10, Leapmotor's global C-segment electric SUV based on the LEAP3.5 architecture, is now locally assembled in a single Design variant.
It is equipped with a 67.1kWh battery, offering up to 434km of WLTP-rated range.
Buyers can choose from Starry Night Blue, Tundra Grey, Metallic Black and Light White, all paired with a Dark Grey interior featuring OEKO-TEX Standard 100-certified upholstery.
Leapmotor aposted record global deliveries of 103,129 vehicles in August, up 80.72 per cent year-on-year.
This marked its fifth consecutive monthly delivery record and pushed cumulative deliveries for the first eight months of 2026 to 560,883 units, up 70.55 per cent year-on-year.

Title: Elderly man who allegedly slashed wife over TV volume remanded 4 days
Article:
KOTA TINGGI:An elderly man suspected of slashing his wife's right hand with a machete at Taman Desa Sejahtera here on Saturday has been remanded for four days from yesterday to assist in investigations.
The remand order for the man, who is in his 70s, was issued by the Kota Tinggi Magistrate's Court to facilitate further investigations under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a weapon.
Kota Tinggi Police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the incident at 9.30pm was believed to have followed an argument over the television volume, which the victim, also in her 70s, allegedly had turned up too high.
The suspect, who was intoxicated, then allegedly attacked the victim with the machete.
He said the victim sustained a small wound, about one centimetre long, to her right hand and was treated at Kota Tinggi Hospital.
She is reported to be in stable condition, he added.

Title: Cops hunt 10 men after 2 Shah Alam brawls, 1 death
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Police are hunting 10 men believed to be involved in two separate group fights here last month, one of which resulted in a death.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the men, aged between 23 and 46, were being sought to assist investigations into separate incidents in Alam Megah on Aug 25 and Taman Sri Muda on Aug 14.
He said a 23-year-old man died in the group fight in Alam Megah and was found to have six previous records involving drug offences.
"In the Taman Sri Muda case, a man was seriously injured after being attacked by two men using machetes and threatened in a group fight involving sharp weapons or objects resembling firearms," he said at a press conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters here today.
Shazeli said police had arrested 21 men, aged between 23 and 46, in a series of raids and arrests in Shah Alam, Klang, Muar and Iskandar Puteri, Johor, between Aug 14 and 28.
"Checks on their records found that several of those detained had various previous criminal and drug-related records," he said.
Meanwhile, Shazeli said police did not rule out the possibility that the suspects in the two cases were linked to gangsterism, although the groups involved were not the same.
He urged anyone with information on the 10 suspects still at large in connection with the two cases to come forward and assist investigations.
He said the Alam Megah case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code, while the Taman Sri Muda case was being investigated under Section 148 of the Penal Code.

Title: Gas Malaysia, Petronas Gas team up on potential Yan pipeline
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gas Malaysia Bhd has signed a joint study and collaboration agreement with Petronas Gas Bhd (PetGas) to develop an onshore lateral pipeline to facilitate the regasification terminal project in Yan, Kedah.
Gas Malaysia, in a filing with Bursa Malaysia, said the agreement sets out a framework for both parties to conduct a feasibility study and related activities for the proposed lateral pipeline.
"The feasibility study is intended to assess the technical, operational and commercial viability of the proposed pipeline interconnection, including engineering design, land acquisition requirements and other technical assessments required to support PetGas confirmation on the proposed interconnection.
"The outcome of the study will provide Gas Malaysia with information required to progress the project and to facilitate the relevant submission to the Energy Commission in accordance with the letter to proceed," it said.
Subject to achieving a final investment decision and obtaining the requisite regulatory and corporate approvals, the project may contribute to the company's future earnings, it added.
Gas Malaysia's share price rose two sen or 0.4 per cent to close at RM5, valuing the company at RM6.42 billion.

Title: Hextar Portfolio raises Hextar Retail stake, triggers mandatory offer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hextar Portfolio Sdn Bhd's conditional voluntary takeover offer for Hextar Retail Bhd has turned into a mandatory offer after acquiring an additional 4.82 per cent stake.
Hextar Portfolio bought an additional 22.41 million shares on the open market, raising its stake in Hextar Retail to about 35.4 per cent.
Following the acquisition, Hextar Portfolio now holds 164.7 million shares in Hextar Retail, according to an announcement made through RHB Investment Bank Bhd.
The latest share purchases triggered a mandatory takeover offer for all remaining Hextar Retail shares not already owned by Hextar Portfolio, the ultimate offeror and parties acting in concert with them.
The offer notice was first served on Hextar Retail's board on Aug 10 on behalf of Hextar Portfolio through RHB Investment.
Hextar Portfolio is an investment vehicle owned by Datuk Ong Choo Meng that operates within the broader Hextar Group.
Hextar Group is a conglomerate spanning multiple listed entities and diverse business sectors.

Title: Malaysia, Australia team up on drones to boost maritime surveillance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia and Australia have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on remotely piloted aircraft systems (RPAS) to expand maritime surveillance and enforcement capabilities across the country's vast waters.
The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) said the cooperation would leverage Australia's expertise in drone technology and extensive maritime operational experience, alongside Malaysia's understanding of its maritime environment and enforcement requirements.
The MoU provides a framework for cooperation in developing and safely integrating RPAS technology into MMEA operations.
MMEA director-general Maritime Admiral Datuk Mohd Rosli Abdullah said the technology could serve as a force multiplier by providing aerial surveillance support and extending the agency's coverage of maritime areas.
"The use of RPAS technology has the potential to become an important element in expanding maritime monitoring and surveillance capabilities, particularly in vast and challenging waters.
"Strategic cooperation with Australia also provides opportunities to share expertise, experience and best practices in developing a capability that is practical, safe and suited to MMEA's operational requirements," he said.
The cooperation comes as Malaysia faces various maritime security challenges, including cross-border crime, incursions, smuggling and other unlawful activities at sea.
MMEA said RPAS could complement existing assets and personnel by providing aerial surveillance and expanding the agency's coverage, strengthening decision-making and operational capabilities.
The agency said the MoU was the second involving MMEA and the Australian government, following the signing of an MoU on Maritime Enforcement Cooperation on Nov 28 last year, with Australia represented by the Maritime Border Command, Australian Border Force.
The latest agreement also provides a more structured framework for both countries to develop operational capabilities together in the long term, further strengthening bilateral ties in maritime security.
MMEA said the signing was in line with its efforts to strengthen surveillance, enforcement and operational readiness through the adoption of modern technology and innovation.
It added that the strategic cooperation reflected both countries' commitment to enhancing their ability to address increasingly dynamic and complex maritime security challenges, while contributing to regional maritime security and stability.
The MoU was signed at MMEA headquarters in Putrajaya today by Rosli and Sean Sullivan, deputy secretary of Australia's Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW).
Also present were MMEA deputy director-general (Logistics) Maritime Vice Admiral Datuk Saiful Lizan Ibrahim; Foreign Ministry Maritime Affairs Department director-general Datin Dr Adina Kamarudin; Australian High Commissioner to Malaysia Danielle Heinecke; senior MMEA officers; and representatives from the Home Ministry, National Security Council, DCCEEW and the Australian High Commission.

Title: HR-V spins 3 times in chain-reaction crash, 4 injured
Article:
TUMPAT: Four people were injured in a five-vehicle crash along Jalan Baru, Wakaf Bharu here about 2pm today.
The incident occurred when a Honda HR-V driven by a man skidded before crashing into a Perodua Axia, followed by a Toyota Vios.
The Honda HR-V then spun three times before crashing into a parked Perodua Alza and the fence of a roadside house.
A Proton Saga FLX was also damaged at the rear after being struck by the Honda HR-V's spare tyre, which was flung from the vehicle.
House owner Teo Hwee Shean, 60, said he was on the second floor when he heard prolonged braking before looking outside and seeing a car coming from the flyover and crashing into two other vehicles.
"The Honda HR-V then spun three times before heading towards my house and crashing into the parked Perodua Alza. The fence of my house was also damaged.
"Shortly after that, smoke emerged from both vehicles, prompting me to immediately move my car parked in the garage as I was worried there might be an explosion," he said when met here today.
The Honda HR-V driver managed to get out through the front passenger door and was believed to have suffered minor injuries, while several other victims were taken to Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZ II) in Kota Bharu.
Hwee Shean said accidents occurred almost daily along the road, although none had been as serious as yesterday's incident or involved his house.
"This time, it was quite serious because it involved many cars and there were injuries. Usually, they are just minor accidents.
"Fortunately, only my house fence was damaged, but the losses are estimated at about RM5,000," he said.

Title: Malaysia's construction upcycle: Opportunities across the field
Article:
MALAYSIA's construction sector is enjoying something it has not experienced consistently for many years: sustained momentum.
Construction sector's economic output as measured by gross domestic product (GDP) at current prices reached RM86.9 billion in 2025, up 11.3 per cent from the preceding year, and the momentum has carried into 2026.
In the first half of this year, construction sector's GDP reached RM45.6 billion, representing year-on-year (y-o-y)growth of 8.5 per cent.
More importantly, this is increasingly looking like a broad investment cycle.
Construction activity spans across all sub-segments and this include residential and commercial developments, industrial facilities, infrastructure, utilities, healthcare and other non-residential projects.
Private-sector activity has also become an increasingly important part of the story.
For investors, the significance is that the construction theme is no longer confined to a handful of mega-project beneficiaries.
The largest contractors remain important bellwethers, but the breadth of activity means there is also room to examine the next tier of companies within the sector.
What The Leaders Tell Us
The achievements of the sector's larger names show how powerful this cycle has become.
Sunway Construction Group Bhd, for example, had secured RM6.86 billion of new orders by August this year while its active tender book is now close to RM14.2 billion.
Its outstanding order book has reached about RM10.5 billion, an all-time high, with data-centre and other advanced-technology projects becoming an increasingly important source of work.
The wider YTL group offers another illustration of where capital expenditure is flowing.
YTL Power International Bhd has continued to expand its digital-infrastructure footprint in Johor, where its Kulai data-centre campus has grown rapidly.
It recently announced plans with JLand Group for a new gigawatt-scale campus at Sedenak Tech Park.
These are not simply company-specific developments; they point to the scale of investment taking place in Malaysia's industrial and digital economy.
Data centres are only one part of the picture. Healthcare, housing, industrial facilities, utilities and transport-related developments are also generating work.
The lesson from the larger groups is therefore less about chasing a particular stock and more about recognising that the construction pipeline is deep enough to create opportunities across different market-capitalisation bands.
Looking Beyond The Big Contractors
The same principle applies further down the market-capitalisationspectrum, where investors can find companies that are benefiting from the broader construction cycle but may not receive the same attention as the sector's largest contractors.
Here, the focus should be on companies with a combination of visible order books, improving financial performance and exposure to resilient areas of construction demand.
Pesona Metro Holdings Bhd is one example. Its outstanding construction order book has grown to about RM2.2 billion following a RM247.5 million contract awarded in July to construct three private hospital blocks in Setia Alam.
This provides the company with substantial visibility over future construction activity and should keep its construction operations well occupied for years to come.
At the same time, the company is already seeing the benefits of stronger project activity, with revenue for the first six months of FY2026 rising 39.2 per cent y-o-y to RM447.9 million, while net profit increased 56.7 per cent to RM26.4 million.
The company also has other attributes that make it worth watching.
As at 30 June 2026, Pesona Metro had RM109.7 million in cash and deposits with licensed financial institutions, alongside RM653.9 million in current assets.
While the group also carries borrowings, its liquidity provides some financial flexibility as it works through its growing project pipeline.
For investors, the appeal is not limited to construction earnings alone.
Metro has also maintained a track record of dividend payments, with an interim dividend of 1.40 sen per share for FY2025, compared with final dividends of 0.75 sen for FY2024 and 0.50 sen for FY2023.
This gives shareholders another potential source of returns beyond capital appreciation and demonstrates that the company is also returning value to shareholders as its earnings grow.
Its acquisition of a 51 per cent stake in property developer Gaya Kuasa SdnBhd in 2024 created a second significant earnings pillar.
The flagship REN Residensi development has a gross development value of about RM810 million and has recorded encouraging take-up.
The impact is already visible. Property development has become a substantial contributor to group revenue and earnings during the first half of FY2026, providing diversification from the traditionally lower-margin construction business.
However, a large order book should not be viewed as an automatic indicator of future returns.
Investors still need to assess the quality and margins of secured contracts, project execution, working-capital requirements and cash conversion.
The ability to translate order-book growth into sustainable earnings and cash flow ultimately matters more than the headline size of the pipeline.
Execution Still Separates Winners From tTe Rest
The sector's outlook is encouraging, but investors should remain selective.
Labour and material costs, subcontractor performance, project delays, working-capital requirements and competitive tendering can all erode construction margins.
Companies expanding into property or other adjacent businesses also take on different operating risks.
This is why the current cycle should be viewed as an opportunity set rather than a blanket buy signal.
Investors need to watch margins, cash conversion cycle, balance-sheet discipline, project execution and the ability to replenish their order books without sacrificing returns.
Malaysia's construction upcycle is therefore bigger than any single company.
The large contractors may capture the headlines and mega projects, but a sustained and broad-based investment cycle can also lift capable smaller players.
For investors willing to look beyond the biggest names, the opportunity lies in identifying companies that can turn unusually strong industry conditions into durable earnings.
* The writer is managing director of Datametrics Research and Information Centre Sdn Bhd. The views expressed are his own.

Title: Police, Media Prima strengthen strategic collaboration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police and Media Prima Bhd have strengthened their strategic collaboration through the PDRM-Media Prima Strategic Communication Collaboration Programme to boost mutual understanding and curb the spread of false news.
Inspector-General of Police, Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, said police value its cooperation with the media, which it regards as the "eyes and ears" of the community, with the police serving as the bulwark of the rule of law.
He said transparency and accuracy in message delivery are the keys to facing the challenges of modern-day crime and increasingly complex cyber threats.
"In facing the threats of modern crime and increasingly sophisticated cyberspace challenges, synergy between the media and the authorities is a need which cannot be compromised. We cannot work in silo.
"Through this programme, police personnel can understand the realities of the fast-paced world of the media, while our media friends can also better understand the strict procedures police have to adhere to in handling sensitive cases and information on public safety," he said.
Khalid was speaking at the programme's closing ceremony at Bukit Aman, here today.
Also present were Media Prima Group Chairman Datuk Seri (Dr) Syed Hussian Aljunid; Media Prima News and Current Affairs Group Managing Editor Jasbant Singh; and Datuk Farrah Naz Abdul Karim, who is Media Prima NCA Deputy Group Managing Editor and New Straits Times Group Editor.
The programme, which began with a briefing on Media Prima operations, was followed by two interactive forums moderated by Buletin TV3 presenter Nur Farah Nabilah Mohammad Wazer.
[[nid:1527785]]
The first forum, titled 'PDRM & Media Saling Melengkapi' (PDRM and Media Prima Complete One Another), featured Jasbant, Farrah Naz and TV3 News Editor Ing Boon Seng.
The second forum, titled 'Perkongsian Wartawan Lapangan' (Insights from Journalists in the Field), featured veteran crime journalists Mohd Jamilul Anbia Md Denin, Safeek Affendy Razali and Hafidzul Hilmi Mohd Noor, before concluding with a press conference simulation exercise.
Meanwhile, Syed Hussian, who is also an honorary assistant commissioner of police, underscored Media Prima's continued commitment as the police's strategic partner to empower the public safety narrative.
Media Prima, he said, remains ready to contribute its expertise and help in terms of training, information dissemination and media support to aid the police.
"Through this exposure, our friends in the police are able to gain insight into the perspectives of media practitioners, while the media, in turn, can better understand the constraints, meticulousness and legal procedures observed by the police.
"Media Prima is committed to ensuring that every effort by the police to uphold law and order in the country is communicated to the public accurately, transparently and effectively," he said.
He also expressed hope that such collaborative platforms and training programmes would continue to be organised on a sustained basis for the well-being of the people and the nation's sovereignty.

Title: Ringgit ends marginally lower against US dollar after strong US jobs data
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed slightly lower on Monday after the United States posted strong non-farm payrolls (NFP) data and ahead of a US inflation report later this week.
The US NFP data last Friday came in at 162,000 in August, well above the consensus forecast of 55,000.
At 6pm, the ringgit inched down to 4.0440/0485 against the US dollar from last Friday's close of 4.0425/0465.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the market is eyeing the US consumer price index (CPI) due on Friday.
"The US CPI report, which is due on Friday, will be the factor that will shape market sentiment as the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members will reconvene next week to decide the Fed Funds Rate.
"Apart from that, Fed staff will share their latest macroeconomic variables such as the gross domestic product, inflation rate, unemployment and the Fed Funds Rate," he told Bernama.
The next FOMC meeting is scheduled for Sept 15-16.
At the close, the ringgit ended lower against a basket of major currencies.
The ringgit slipped against the euro to 4.6991/7044 from last Friday's 4.6962/7008, eased against the British pound to 5.4736/4796 from 5.4663/4717, and weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.6173/6204 from 2.5832/5860.
The ringgit also traded lower against regional currencies.
It inched down against the Philippine peso to 6.46/6.47 from 6.45/6.46 last Friday and declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.1943/1981 from 3.1888/1923.
It fell against the Thai baht to 12.3041/3231 from 12.2693/2863 and also traded lower against the Indonesian rupiah at 229.2/229.6 from 229.1/229.4 at the previous close.

Title: Vestland unit bags RM263.7mil job in Kelantan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Vestland Bhd's unit Vestland Infra Sdn Bhd has been awarded a contract by Johnson Fluid Engineering Sdn Bhd to build a dual-function sheet pile wall and bridge works in Kelantan valued at RM263.7 million.
The construction works, scheduled to start on Sept 21, are expected to be completed within 19 months.
Vestland joint managing director Datuk Liew Foo Heen said this is its sixth contract win for the year and represents its strategic expansion into flood mitigation and infrastructure development.
"It strengthens our capabilities in this sector, positioning the group to pursue larger and more complex infrastructure and climate resilience projects," said Liew.
The latest contract brings Vestland's contract wins for this year to RM1.1 billion and strengthens its total outstanding order book to RM1.5 billion.
Vestland's closed 1.5 sen or 1.6 per cent to 92 sen, valuing the company at RM864.14 million.

Title: Former TV station assistant director jailed six months over RM28,000 bribes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former assistant director of a television station was sentenced to six months' jail and fined RM20,000 by the Shah Alam Sessions Court after being found guilty of two charges of receiving RM28,000 seven years ago.
Judge Datuk Mohd Nasir Nordin handed down the sentence to Suhaila Md Zaini, 47, after finding her guilty under Section 165 of the Penal Code which concerns a public servant receiving any valuable thing in the course of his or her duty.
He also ordered her to servce six months in jail for each charge if she failed to pay the fine.
According to the charges, Suhaila received RM10,000 from a company on July 9, 2019.
She was also charged with receiving RM18,000 in cash from an individual between April 17 and June 5, 2019, without consideration, knowing that the money was related to her official duties as a programme producer at a local television station.
The court found that the accused's defence that the RM10,000 was a loan was an afterthought, as the repayment was only made after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission began its investigation in October 2019.
The court also found that the use of a third-party account to make the payment indicated an attempt to conceal the offence.
Her defence that the RM18,000 was used for expenses and payments related to programmes at a local television station was also rejected as it was not material to the charges.
The court allowed a stay of execution pending her appeal to the Shah Alam High Court and increased her bail to RM10,000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: On a Kyiv maternity ward, babies are born during air raids
Article:
THE air raid alert in Kyiv was live, warning of approaching Russian jet-propelled drones, but fortunately there were no explosions nearby during the final phase of Alyona Bohatyrenko's labour.
"I gave birth during an air alert!" beamed the 32-year-old, as she lay in her hospital bed cradling her baby daughter minutes after she was born.
"None of this is normal, but ... you get used to it somehow."
Doctors at Kyiv City Maternity Hospital No. 2 took a calculated risk by delivering Bohatyrenko's baby on the ward while the skies over the city were under threat.
The same was true for Yuliia Ishchuk, 26, who also gave birth there last Wednesday.
Her husband, 30-year-old serviceman Vitalii Ishchuk, recalled the moment the couple knew the baby was close.
"At three in the morning, the waters broke, but we hadn't packed anything, and nothing was ready," he said. Kyiv was under attack, as it has been almost non-stop since Aug 27, when Russia significantly escalated its bombing campaign.
"We thought the house was going to be blown to pieces. We called an ambulance; they came, and everything turned out fine."
In an escalating air war between Ukraine and Russia, in which each side is pounding the other's energy and logistical assets to force an advantage, Moscow has fired swarms of high-speed jet drones that are more destructive than older models.
In the last fortnight, air attacks in Kyiv and the surrounding region have been around-the-clock rather than mainly at night, disrupting everyday life for millions of residents.
[[nid:1527759]]
Officials say conditions are likely to worsen as winter sets in and Russia targets Ukraine's energy system that provides electricity, heating and running water.
Russia says its attacks have a military purpose; Ukraine says they are designed to break civilian morale and persuade the government to give up territory.
For both young families at the hospital, growing threats are forcing them to consider moving into safer accommodation in Kyiv or away from the city altogether.
"We'll have to move somewhere to find better shelter - not a basement in a school or a store - that's no shelter at all," said Vitalii Ishchuk.
Bohatyrenko ruled out moving overseas, but added:
"We're thinking about going somewhere this winter after all. We'll have to see how things go, because based on the forecasts, it'll be very difficult to stay in Kyiv this winter with a small child."
Beneath the hospital, several pregnant women walked into a shelter with their partners in response to a fresh air raid warning.
Yuliia Kukhar, 29, said that she had only noticed a handful of women with her on the maternity ward.
"No one wants to give birth," she told Reuters.
Ukraine is facing a demographic crisis, with birth rates plunging because of economic factors before the full-scale invasion and, since February 2022, due to partners serving in the military and concerns over the country's security.
Kukhar was expecting her third child. After two daughters, she had thought it would be good to have a boy, but the war, and the risk men faced of being called up to serve, made her think twice.
"We wanted a boy. But there's a war going on, and I don't need a boy. Let's just have girls."
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: Anak Krakatau volcanic ash hampers efforts to induce rain, further eruptions possible
Article:
JAKARTA: Efforts to induce rain following eruptions at Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau are being hampered by volcanic ash, as authorities warned that further eruptions could occur at any time amid high seismic activity.
In its latest monitoring update covering 6 am to noon local time, the Geological Agency recorded 17 low-frequency earthquakes, 23 hybrid earthquakes, nine harmonic tremors and continuous tremor, while the volcano remained at Level III, the second-highest level in Indonesia's four-tier volcano alert system.
The agency said it continued to closely monitor the volcano through the Anak Krakatau Volcano Observation Posts in Pasauran, Banten, and Kalianda, Lampung.
"All monitoring data are analysed and evaluated by volcanologists at the Geological Agency," it said in its latest social media post on Monday.
Anak Krakatau has recorded a series of eruptions since Friday, sending volcanic ash across parts of western Indonesia and disrupting air travel, while the Geological Agency reported on Sunday that a prolonged eruption episode lasting about 25 hours had subsided.
However, the impact of the volcanic ash continued to be felt on Monday, with National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) chief Suharyanto saying it had spread across at least four provinces, namely Jakarta, West Java, Lampung and South Sumatra.
He said BNPB had been trying since Sunday to induce rain through weather modification operations (OMC), but the effort was hampered by the volcanic ash, which had also forced the temporary closure of eight airports and prevented the operation from proceeding.
He said BNPB was considering three airports as bases for conducting the OMC: Pondok Cabe Airport near Jakarta once conditions allowed, Kertajati International Airport in West Java or Ahmad Yani International Airport in Semarang, Central Java.
"We have moved the weather modification aircraft from Kalimantan and it is now in Semarang. We can at least conduct OMC from there because Ahmad Yani Airport in Semarang is not closed," he said during an online meeting on the latest disaster response chaired by President Prabowo Subianto and streamed live on Monday.
Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) chief Teuku Faisal Fathani at the same meeting said potential cloud formation and light to moderate rain were expected over areas affected by the Anak Krakatau eruption from Sept 9, providing conditions that could be enhanced through the OMC.
He said the operation remained challenging as volcanic ash could damage aircraft engines, reduce visibility and interfere with aircraft navigation and sensors, while operating farther from the Sunda Strait would reduce its effectiveness.
"The farther from the Sunda Strait, the less effective the weather modification operation will be," he said, adding that operations from Ahmad Yani Airport in Semarang, for example, would have a more limited reach in inducing rain around the Sunda Strait.

Title: Volcanic ash eases, but Indonesian airports remains closed
Article:
JAKARTA: Volcanic ash conditions around several Indonesian airports showed signs of improvement, with tests at four airports finding no ash at ground level.
Transport Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said four consecutive ground-level tests at Soekarno-Hatta had returned negative for volcanic ash, but authorities were holding off reopening Indonesia's main international gateway until they were satisfied that conditions were safe.
"We have conducted four tests, or paper tests, at Soekarno-Hatta Airport and found the results to be negative. However, we are not immediately reopening it because we want to be absolutely certain," he said during a briefing with President Prabowo Subianto on Monday.
Dudy said additional caution was necessary as wind directions had shifted during the volcanic ash episode, potentially changing the direction in which ash from Anak Krakatau was dispersed.
He said eight airports affected by Anak Krakatau's volcanic ash had initially been temporarily closed, with Atung Bungsu Airport in Pagar Alam, South Sumatra, reopening at 9am today after an assessment found it was no longer affected.
The remaining seven airports, namely Soekarno-Hatta, Halim Perdanakusuma, Radin Inten II, Budiarto Curug, Husein Sastranegara, M. Taufik Kiemas and Pondok Cabe, remained temporarily closed until 6pm local time today.
As of 9am today, volcanic ash had affected about 2,300 flights and 270,337 passengers since Sept 5, including cancelled, delayed and diverted flights, according to Transport Ministry data.
Of these, 1,397 flights involving about 177,579 passengers were affected at airports that had been temporarily closed, while another 922 flights involving about 92,758 passengers were affected at other airports due to flight route adjustments.
Meanwhile, Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) chief Teuku Faisal Fathani said at the same briefing that ground-level ash detection tests at Halim Perdanakusuma, Husein Sastranegara and Budiarto Curug airports had returned negative.
"We can see that volcanic ash at higher altitudes, reaching up to 50,000 feet, has moved away towards the Indian Ocean, while ash at lower altitudes, from the surface up to 15,000 feet, remains around the affected areas," he said.
He said BMKG was continuing to coordinate with the Darwin Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre (VAAC), which covers Southeast Asia, Australia and surrounding areas, as authorities assessed conditions for reopening the affected airports.
He said BMKG had also launched a continuously updated aviation weather website where the public could check which airports were closed, the duration of the closures and subsequent changes to their operational status.
Meanwhile, Dudy said Kertajati, Juanda, Ahmad Yani, Adi Soemarmo and Yogyakarta International airports had been prepared as alternatives, while 10 airports were being readied for 24-hour operations to accommodate diverted flights and accelerate the recovery of flight schedules.
He said airlines were also adjusting operations through alternative airports, with Garuda Indonesia and Lion Air operating services through Kertajati, while Singapore Airlines would deploy larger Airbus A350 aircraft through Juanda and Yogyakarta to accommodate more passengers.
Dudy said passengers whose flights were cancelled were entitled to full refunds, while immigration authorities were providing flexibility for foreigners who exceeded their permitted stay due to the disruption.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: More than 1,000 open burning cases recorded in Pahang this year
Article:
KUANTAN: Pahang recorded a significant increase in open burning cases in the first eight months of this year, with 1,003 cases reported compared to 658 during the same period last year.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department director Datuk Mohd Razam Taja Rahim said about 2,721.88ha of land were affected, more than double that of last year, at 1,162.83ha.
"A total of 619 cases recorded in Pahang this year involved bush and grass fires. Dry areas with overgrown bushes can easily catch fire and require special attention," he said in a statement.
Razam Taja cautioned the public against taking open burning incidents lightly, particularly during dry conditions.
"The public should refrain from open burning, particularly from burning rubbish, dry leaves, overgrown bushes or agricultural waste. During dry conditions, a small fire can spread and develop into a larger blaze within a short time.
"Negligence, such as discarding cigarette butts, leaving burning embers unattended or using fire sources near dry vegetation, could also trigger fires," he said.
Razam said the public should not resort to burning rubbish or clearing areas by fire, as flames could spread to neighbouring areas, farms, forests or homes.
"Actions that may seem minor can have serious consequences for safety, property and the environment," he said.

Title: 3 Sarawak areas record very unhealthy API readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today.
Data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed Serian recording the highest reading at 266, followed by Samarahan (238) and Kuching (203).
Meanwhile, 37 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy API readings, ranging from 106 to 196.
Sarawak recorded the highest number of areas with unhealthy air quality, with Sarikei recording a reading of 196, followed by Sri Aman (194), Sibu (183), Mukah (179), Samalaju (175), ILP Miri and Miri (167 each), Bintulu (166) and Limbang (141).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded an API reading of 187, followed by Shah Alam (166), Klang (159), Banting (158), Kuala Selangor (157) and Petaling Jaya (156).
Perak recorded unhealthy readings in Seri Manjung (165), Tasek Ipoh (163), Tanjung Malim (160), Pegoh Ipoh (155) and Taiping (152).
Nilai (162), Seremban (160) and Port Dickson (120) in Negri Sembilan also recorded unhealthy air quality.
Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 160, while Batu Muda (158) and Cheras (156) in Kuala Lumpur were also at unhealthy levels.
In Sabah, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded a reading of 155, followed by Kota Kinabalu (152) and Kimanis (150).
Johor recorded unhealthy readings in Segamat (155), Batu Pahat (153), Tangkak (151) and Kluang (108).
Meanwhile, Bukit Rambai (155), Alor Gajah (153) and Bandaraya Melaka (106) in Melaka, as well as Labuan (154), also recorded unhealthy air quality.
A total of 26 areas recorded moderate API readings, while Langkawi, Kedah (49), and Kangar, Perlis (45), recorded good air quality.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and above 300 hazardous.
