Title: 17ha peatland blaze in Pengerang expected to take 2 days to put out
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Firefighters battling a peatland blaze along the Sebana Cove-Punggai bypass in Pengerang are expected to need another two days to completely extinguish the fire, which has burned 17 hectares.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said firefighters had so far put out flames over 10 hectares of the affected area.
She said the department received a distress call at 5pm yesterday, prompting the deployment of 18 personnel from the Sebana Cove and Punggai fire stations.
"The fire has spread to the other side of the road, bringing the total area affected to 17 hectares.
"If the weather remains relatively calm and there are no strong winds, we expect the situation to be brought under control and the firefighting operation to be completed within another two days," she said after inspecting the operation today.
Siti Rohani said human activity could not be ruled out as a possible cause, particularly amid the current hot and dry weather.
She urged the public to refrain from open burning, saying even a small fire could quickly spread under such conditions.
Firefighters are using an excavator to dig trenches to contain the blaze, while water is being sprayed directly onto the affected areas.
Meanwhile, Tanjung Surat assemblyman Aznan Tamin, who spent about an hour inspecting the operation, also urged residents to stop open burning during the hot and dry spell.
"The fire started small but spread rapidly due to strong winds and the extreme heat.
"I strongly urge those in the area not to conduct open burning. Let us stop for the next month or two to prevent more fires," he said.
Aznan also urged parents to monitor their children and limit outdoor activities, while schools should temporarily suspend outdoor activities to safeguard pupils' health and safety.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore's high ministerial salaries under scrutiny in parliament this week
Article:
SINGAPORE: Top ministers in Singapore will discuss ministerial salaries in parliament on Tuesday, a sensitive and closely watched topic in the city-state, where political office comes with high rates of pay in order to attract talent and deter graft.
Singapore pays its political leaders the highest salary in the world, with a junior minister taking home S$1.1 million (US$868,056) annually and the prime minister earning S$2.2 million (US$1.74 million) a year.
The salaries have not been adjusted since 2012, when ministers took a 36 per cent pay cut to allay public discontent about how much they earned.
High ministerial salaries are a sensitive issue among the population, where the median monthly income was just S$5,775 in 2025.
Meanwhile, inflation crept up to two per cent in July, with the central bank expecting the figure to remain elevated until the second half of 2027.
According to data from non-profit PoliticalSalaries.com, the Hong Kong chief executive is the second-highest earner globally with US$719,000 annually, followed by the Swiss president at US$606,000.
In comparison, the British prime minister makes US$230,000 while President Donald Trump earns US$400,000.
After the 2012 pay cut, the government reviewed salaries again in 2017 but chose not to adopt a committee recommendation to hike.
A second review due in 2023 was deferred till now because of economic uncertainty.
On Tuesday, Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and Coordinating Minister for Public Services Chan Chun Sing will provide the government's response to a committee's recommendations on ministerial salaries.
Lawmakers will debate the issue later in the week.
Singapore uses the salary of the top 1,000 Singaporean earners as a benchmark for ministerial pay, saying the qualities and abilities of the top 1,000 "reflect the desired calibre of the people whom Singapore needs for good government", according to the website of the country's Public Service Division.
The high salaries are meant to attract top talent and prevent corruption, and cases of graft by senior officials have been rare.
In a recent case, former transport minister S. Iswaran was jailed in 2024 for obstructing justice and receiving more than US$300,000 worth of gifts.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MAHB: 41 flights to Jakarta cancelled following Anak Krakatau eruption
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — A total of 41 flights to Jakarta (CGK) were cancelled at airports nationwide today following the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport due to volcanic ash from the Anak Krakatau eruption, according to Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd (MAHB).
It said the cancellations involved flights scheduled between 6.45 am and 11.55 pm today.
“The highest number of cancellations was recorded at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), with 30 flights, comprising 20 at Terminal 1 and 10 at Terminal 2,” it said.
The airport operator said that Penang International Airport recorded seven cancellations, followed by Subang Airport with two, while Kuching International Airport and Kota Kinabalu International Airport recorded one cancellation each.
No cancellations were recorded at Kota Bharu Airport.
The cancellations followed the temporary closure of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport after volcanic ash from the Anak Krakatau eruption affected flight operations. — Bernama

Title: Four-month old baby dies after found unconscious at Dungun childcare centre
Article:
DUNGUN,  Sept 7 — A four-month-old baby girl died after being found unconscious at a childcare centre in Bandar Al Muktafi Billah Shah (AMBS) near here today.
Dungun police chief Supt Nik Ab Halim Nik Mat said police received a report on the incident at 3.41 pm.
He said preliminary investigations found that the baby had been dropped off at the centre by her mother at about 8 am in good health.
“At about 10 am, staff at the centre found the victim unconscious after she had slept and been fed milk.
“She was taken to Durian Mas Health Clinic before being referred to Dungun Hospital,” he said in a statement today.
Nik Ab Halim said medical personnel at the hospital conducted examinations and resuscitation efforts, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), but the baby was pronounced dead at about 12.45 pm.
He said no visible physical injuries were found during an initial examination of the body.
“However, the exact cause of death has yet to be determined, and a post-mortem examination will be conducted,” he said.
He added that police had identified the two caregivers on duty at the time and would record their statements, along with those of the victim’s parents and other relevant witnesses.
Police will also obtain medical reports and professional opinions as part of the investigation.
The police have opened an investigation under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 to determine whether there were elements of negligence or abandonment while the victim was under the care of the childcare centre. — Bernama

Title: Police: Six missing Gunung Trans Gerah hikers contacted, safe for now
Article:
IPOH, Sept 7 — Six individuals, including two children, who were reported missing while trekking along the Gunung Trans Gerah trail in Lojing, Gua Musang, have managed to make contact this afternoon and reported that they are safe.
Gerik police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said information regarding the group’s condition was received at about 5.30 pm today after a family member managed to contact one of the mountain guides accompanying the group.
“We can only confirm that the victims have been contacted, and they informed their family members that they are safe.
“However, we have not found the victims yet because they are still at the climbing location, and the rescue team will move to meet them before bringing them out either today or tomorrow, as they are believed to be within the Perak area,” he said when contacted today.
He added that the exact condition of all the victims, including the possibility of any injuries, cannot be confirmed until the rescue team successfully locates them.
Abdul Samad said the method for extracting the group - whether by land or air - will be determined based on their condition and location after the SAR team manages to meet the victims.
“If conditions permit, we will see whether to use a helicopter or land routes; we will assess the situation when the rescue team meets the hikers later. The SAR process will only end after all the victims are successfully brought down,” he said.
Previously, Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, and his wife Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, along with their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, as well as two mountain guides Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43, were reported missing after trekking the mountain on Aug 29.
They were reported to have failed to exit the forest by their scheduled date of Sept 3, and family members lodged a police report yesterday.
Meanwhile, Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said smoke signals detected during an aerial survey by a JBPM helicopter helped the SAR team estimate the location of the six missing hikers in the forested area of Pos Kemar here.
Based on the aerial survey, the location of the hikers was estimated to be about an hour’s journey from Kem Kulim. The JBPM Mi-17 aircraft from the Subang Air Base, which arrived at Pos Kemar at 4.30 pm today, brought 11 SAR personnel comprising five JBPM personnel, four Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) personnel, one Forestry Department officer and one mountain guide.
“The SAR team was also assisted by 14 Malaysian Mountain Guides (MGM), who entered through the hiking trail, bringing the total number of SAR personnel to 25,” she said in a statement today.
Sayani said based on assessments and discussions between JBPM and the Forestry Department, as well as information from the hikers’ last short message service (SMS) on Sept 1, the group was believed to have used the route via Gunung Bieh, Gunung Sepat, Gunung Belatoh, Kampung Agek, Gunung Bongok and subsequently Pos Kemar.
The Forestry Department also received information at 5.15 pm today regarding a message from the hikers informing that all of them had arrived safely at Gunung Bongok.
“The SAR team is now moving to meet the missing hikers in the area, and they are expected to regroup at Kem Kulim tonight. The decision on whether they will be brought out tonight or spend the night at Kem Kulim will depend on their condition and the situation at the location,” she said.
Sayani said the estimated journey for the SAR team, together with the hikers, from Kem Kulim to Pos Kemar was between three and four hours. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians urged to register on Foreign Ministry’s E-Konsular as precaution, though not mandatory
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Recent developments around the world, arising from natural disasters and geopolitical situations, have increased the need for Malaysians to register with the Foreign Affairs Ministry’s
e-Konsular
system to provide information on their whereabouts.
For instance, when major floods occurred in Nepal last month, information on Malaysians there was obtained only from their relatives back home and travel agencies used by Malaysians travelling to the country.
The
e-Konsular
system helps Malaysian diplomatic missions around the world provide assistance more quickly in the event of an emergency.
Registration can be done at
https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my/login
or by downloading the e-Konsular application via a QR code.
According to the
ekonsular.kln.gov.my
website, the registration is intended to systematically record the whereabouts of Malaysians overseas.
Consular assistance for Malaysians abroad is one of the efforts by the Foreign Ministry, also known as Wisma Putra, to safeguard their welfare in all circumstances.
It covers cases involving the death, detention or disappearance of Malaysians abroad; deposits of money by family members for those requiring consular assistance; as well as other disasters and emergencies.
A survey of posts on the social media platform Threads found that many Malaysian users shared their experiences registering with
e-Konsular
while abroad.
Threads user
icecoffeeonearth
suggested that Malaysians email the Malaysian Embassy in the country they are visiting if the
e-Konsular
application cannot be accessed.
Another Threads user,
solehahtravel
, said that although registration is not mandatory, registering with
e-Konsular
would at least make it easier for Malaysians to deal with the relevant authorities.
“Misfortune can happen without warning…,” said the Threads user solehahtravel. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia deploying DNA experts to identify disaster victims, pending Nepal’s go-ahead
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept  7 —Malaysia is awaiting approval from the Nepalese government to deploy deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) experts to assist in identifying the bodies of disaster victims in the country.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said Malaysia had submitted a request to deploy the experts, with the DNA identification process expected to begin after search and rescue (SAR) operations conclude.
He said the expertise was needed to match DNA samples taken from recovered bodies with samples provided by the families of Malaysian citizens who remain missing.
“There are bodies that have been recovered but were immediately buried due to a lack of adequate facilities.
“We need DNA to match against the DNA samples from the families of the Malaysian citizens. The process will be carried out once the search and rescue (SAR) operation concludes,” he told a press conference following a luncheon held in conjunction with the working visit of Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow here today.
Last Saturday, Mohamad announced that DNA samples had been successfully collected from the next of kin of the 55 Malaysians who remain unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal.
Meanwhile, he said the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), which is currently en route to the affected areas, would assist the Nepalese authorities in efforts to locate the missing victims.
Mohamad expressed hope that the team’s presence would contribute to search and recovery efforts for those still classified as missing.
Yesterday, the SMART MAS01 team, deployed as part of the Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) mission to Nepal, arrived safely at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu at noon local time.
The National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA) said the team completed arrival procedures and mission protocols by 4.30 pm local time, including logistics clearance and personnel manifest verification.
The team comprises 11 SMART members and officers carrying 12.4 tonnes of SAR equipment, including rescue gear, detection tools, communication systems, high-capacity drones and specialised tunnel rescue equipment, as well as a four-wheel-drive vehicle and a 10-tonne truck. — Bernama

Title: Elderly man remanded four days for slashing wife’s hand
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 7 — An elderly man suspected of slashing his wife’s right hand with a machete at Taman Desa Sejahtera here today has been remanded for four days from yesterday to assist in investigations.
The remand order for the man, who is in his 70s, was issued by the Kota Tinggi Magistrate’s Court to facilitate further investigations under Section 324 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt with a weapon.
Kota Tinggi Police chief Supt Yusof Othman said the incident at about 9.30 pm was believed to have followed an argument over the television volume, which the victim, also in her 70s, allegedly had turned up too high.
The suspect, who was intoxicated, then allegedly attacked the victim with the machete.
He said the victim sustained a small wound, about one centimetre long, to her right hand and was treated at Kota Tinggi Hospital.
She is reported to be in stable condition, he added. — Bernama

Title: Police tracking down 10 suspects to assist in murder, gang fight in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — Police are tracking down 10 men to assist in the investigation of two separate fight cases in Taman Alam Megah and Taman Sri Muda here last month.
Selangor Police Chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said of that number, seven men are wanted to assist in the investigation of a fight in Taman Alam Megah that resulted in the death of a 23-year-old local man on Aug 25.
Meanwhile, three others are wanted in connection with a case where a man was attacked with a machete and threatened with an object resembling a firearm in Taman Sri Muda last month.
“All of the individuals involved are aged between 23 and 46, and those still at large are wanted to assist in ongoing investigations,” he said at a press conference at the Selangor Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) here today.
He said following both cases, police conducted a series of raids in Shah Alam, as well as Lenga and Iskandar Puteri, Johor, between Aug 14 and 28.
As a result of the raids, police successfully arrested 21 local men aged between 23 and 46, and also seized various weapons including seven machetes, two cable cutters, nine cars, and three motorcycles.
“Out of the 21 arrested, eight male suspects have been charged in court under Sections 302 and 149 of the Penal Code, while another four men were charged under Section 148 of the same act,” he said.
He said checks also revealed that the victim who died in the Taman Alam Megah case had six past criminal records related to drug offences.
Meanwhile, Shazeli said police do not rule out the possibility that both cases are linked to elements of gangsterism, but involving different factions.
“At the early stage, we believe the case involving the death stems from a turf war, while the other resulted from a misunderstanding.
“Police will not compromise with any individuals involved in gangsterism and will ensure they are all brought to court,” he said.
On Aug 27, Shazeli confirmed that the fight incident in Taman Alam Megah involved a group of individuals resulting in the death of a man, suspected to stem from rivalry between two secret society groups.
Eight men, including two brothers who are members of a secret society group, were hauled to the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court on Sept 4 to face murder charges.
In a separate incident on Aug 13, a local man was seriously injured after reportedly being slashed with a machete during a fight near a petrol station in Taman Sri Muda at around 11 am. — Bernama

Title: Housing Ministry: Check Teduh to check project, developer information before buying property
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The public, particularly prospective homebuyers, are encouraged to check information on developers and housing projects through the TEDUH portal and mobile application before making a purchase decision to reduce the risk of encountering problems later.
The Ministry of Housing and Local Government (KPKT) said TEDUH, developed by the National Housing Department (JPN), is a one-stop platform providing access to information such as developers’ licence status, advertising permit and developer’s licence (APDL), project progress and information related to private housing projects.
“Through the #TEDUHBersama campaign, the ministry aims to cultivate the practice of ‘check before you buy’ among the public, particularly prospective homebuyers, as an initial step to reduce the risk of dealing with unlicensed developers or making purchase decisions without knowing the actual status of a project,” the ministry said in a statement.
It added that the portal also provides facilities to check the status of private housing projects, including projects categorised as delayed, troubled or abandoned, as well as approved selling prices.
Users can also check certain approvals issued by the government, including extensions of time (EOT), verify the authenticity of related documents and submit housing development complaints to JPN for review and further action.
JPN director-general Dr Tan Awang Besar, in the same statement, said the public was advised to conduct checks before purchasing a house as it was one of the biggest financial commitments in a person’s life.
“This simple step is important to help buyers obtain accurate information, make decisions with greater confidence and reduce the risk of encountering problems later,” he said.
TEDUH was launched on Aug 11, 2017, and has since been progressively enhanced as a more comprehensive, transparent and user-friendly housing reference platform.
According to KPKT, the TEDUH portal recorded more than 45 million visitors in total as of August.
The public can access the TEDUH Portal via
teduh.kpkt.gov.my
or use the TEDUH mobile application. — Bernama

Title: Over 26,000 new undergraduates to benefit from RM1,500 PTPTN advance payments
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) continues to strengthen the nation’s higher education empowerment agenda by offering Loan Advance Payments (WPP) totaling RM1,500 to eligible new students to help cover part of the initial preparation costs for admission to public universities and polytechnics.
In a statement, PTPTN said the RM39.7 million scheme benefits 26,457 students entering bachelor’s degree programmes at public universities and polytechnics for the September 2026 intake.
“The WPP is available to Malaysian citizens who opted into the scheme when applying to public higher education institutions via UPUOnline or university websites.
“In addition, applicants’ parents or guardians must be recipients of Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and meet the specified eligibility criteria,” according to the statement.
From WPP’s introduction in 1999 until July 31, more than 1 million students have benefited from the initiative, with an allocation totaling RM1.48 billion, it said.
The agency, which operates under the Higher Education Ministry (MOHE), said applicants can check their offers via the myPTPTN mobile app and collect the cash at Bank Islam branches nationwide starting Sept 4 by presenting their WPP offer letter and MyKad.
“The WPP is valid for two months, from Sept 4 to Nov 3 (Tuesday),” it said, noting that third-party collection is not permitted.
Recently, PTPTN also reached out to students receiving the WPP offer through home visits in Tasek Gelugor, Penang, followed by the WPP handover ceremony for the Bukit Gelugor area, officiated by PTPTN Chairman Datuk Seri Norliza Abdul Rahim.
According to the statement, Norliza said in her speech that PTPTN remains committed to strengthening the higher education agenda by ensuring that access to education financing continues to be empowered and can be enjoyed by all layers of society regardless of background and socio-economic status.
“In line with that aspiration, PTPTN’s WPP is among the strategic initiatives implemented to provide early financial support to students, thereby helping to ease the financial burden on families in making preparations and meeting basic needs before students begin studies at public universities and polytechnics,” she said.
PTPTN also said that students who wish to apply for loans can submit applications online via the myPTPTN application during the application period set by each public university and polytechnic, to ensure applications are processed and approved accordingly.
PTPTN said students must have a National Education Savings Scheme (Simpan SSPN) account, which can be opened through the myPTPTN application, urging them to refer to the Student Affairs Division of their respective universities and polytechnics or contact PTPTN if they have any questions.
It said additional details on loan advances and educational financing can be obtained from the myPTPTN digital application for easier, faster, and safer services. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia rail link: ECRL passenger fares to be known by year-end
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Passenger fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) have not been finalised and an official announcement will be made by the end of this year, said Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL).
MRL said in a statement on the ECRL Facebook page today that a recently recirculated information on social media regarding the passenger fares is inaccurate and has never been verified by any authority.
The company said the official passenger fares for the ECRL will only be announced by the Ministry of Transport Malaysia once the relevant evaluation and approval processes are finalised.
MRL advised the public against making any assumptions or conclusions based on unverified information, and to instead refer to announcements made through official channels of the Ministry of Transport, MRL, and ECRL.
"The ECRL fares will be determined after taking into account the public interest, user affordability, as well as the value and quality of services to be offered,” it said.
MRL said that once operational, travel time between Kota Bharu and Gombak is expected to take around four hours, Kuala Terengganu to Gombak about three hours, and Kuantan to Gombak approximately one hour and 35 minutes.
"The ECRL not only offers a new transport option for the public, but will also transform mobility between the East Coast and the Klang Valley,” it said.
The first phase of the ECRL from Kota Bharu to Gombak is expected to begin operations this December. — Bernama

Title: Minden air quality hits unhealthy level as API rises to 142, says Penang exco
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 7 — Air quality in parts of Penang island reached an unhealthy level today, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading climbing to 142 at 3pm.
Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu said the Minden air-quality monitoring station on the island began recording unhealthy readings at 9am.
“The reading continued to rise, reaching 142 at 3pm,” he said in a statement today.
He said the station recorded readings of between 82 and 142 throughout the day.
Meanwhile, monitoring stations in Seberang Perai, Seberang Jaya and Balik Pulau recorded moderate readings of between 55 and 91.
Minden was the only one of Penang’s four monitoring stations to record unhealthy air quality.
Sundarajoo said Penang’s air quality had generally remained at good to moderate levels between September 4 and 6.
He said preliminary information from the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre showed that 737 hotspots were recorded in Sumatra and another 540 in Kalimantan during the period.
Hotspots were also detected in several Malaysian states.
“The increase in hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan indicates more significant fire activity in the region,” he said.
However, Sundarajoo said hotspot numbers alone could not determine Penang’s air quality.
He said the impact on the state depended on factors such as wind direction and speed, atmospheric conditions and rainfall distribution.
“Intermittent rain had helped keep Penang’s air quality within good to moderate levels during the monitoring period,” he said.
PM₁₀ was identified as the dominant pollutant, although its concentration remained at a moderate level.
He advised the public to monitor official API readings for their respective areas through the Department of Environment’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
He also urged the public not to rely on unverified information or social media posts.
He advised the public to avoid open burning, including burning rubbish, dried leaves and agricultural waste, and to report such activities immediately.
Children, senior citizens and those with respiratory conditions should reduce strenuous outdoor activities if API readings rise.
The public should also reduce the time spent outdoors, keep doors and windows closed, and wear suitable face masks if air quality worsens.
Sundarajoo said the public should avoid activities that could worsen air pollution and reduce unnecessary vehicle use.
He encouraged residents to use public transport, carpool or choose more sustainable ways of travelling.
He said the Department of Environment and other relevant agencies will continue monitoring air quality and regional hotspots.

Title: No cracks in federal unity govt, says Pakatan minister as Umno closes gap with PAS ahead of assembly
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 7 — PKR today denied speculations of turmoil among federal unity government components following developments in Umno’s ties with PAS.
PKR vice-president Datuk Chang Lih Kang said Pakatan Harapan (PH) continues to maintain good relations with BN, despite Umno’s strategic cooperation with PAS.
He said PKR nonetheless keeps a close watch on shifting political dynamics from time to time,
Harian Metro
reported.
“So far, there are no issues, and all Umno ministers still attended last week's Cabinet meeting.
“We discussed national issues seriously, but there was no political chit-chat during the Cabinet meeting.
“We'll see how things unfold, this is a party matter. I can only confirm there is no turmoil in the Cabinet at this point,” Chang was quoted as saying at a press conference after the National Science Challenge Prime Minister's Cup final here.
He was responding to Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi’s earlier statement that
PH would not be invited to Umno’s assembly this week, as PAS had already been invited.
Zahid said Umno would focus on the pros and cons of cooperation rather than finalising any coalition arrangement ahead of the 16th general election.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier said the decision to invite PAS’ top leadership was agreed upon at the party’s supreme council meeting.

Title: Selangor police say investigation into Sunway Lagoon ride gone wrong to take at least three months as it waits for tech report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The investigation into the August 22 roller coaster incident at Sunway Lagoon that injured 10 visitors could take another three to four months.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said this is because investigators are waiting for technical reports from several agencies before they can wrap up the case.
“We estimate it may take three to four months for us to obtain the findings of the investigation. This is because we need technical reports from several agencies involved,” he told a news conference at the Selangor police contingent headquarters in Shah Alam.
He said police were working with the occupational safety and health department (DOSH), Fire and Rescue Department, forensic teams and other agencies on the investigation.
“Police have taken statements from the staff operating the ride, victims and medical officers,” Shazeli said.
The ride accident occurred at about 9pm on August 22 and involved 22 local and foreign visitors aged between 11 and 44, with no deaths reported.
Selangor DOSH previously said a preliminary investigation found the roller coaster had been operating normally before a “sliding failure” about 200m from the disembarkation point triggered its automatic emergency braking system, causing it to stop abruptly.
As of September 2, all visitors treated and placed under observation at hospitals had been discharged.
The roller coaster remains closed pending completion of the investigation.

Title: No seat for Pakatan at annual Umno assembly, but PAS gets red carpet
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Umno will not be inviting its federal government partner Pakatan Harapan (PH) to its general assembly, starting this Wednesday to Saturday.
Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PAS was invited instead, as a reciprocal gesture for the invitation to the Islamist party’s 72nd congress in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, last weekend.
“There's give and take. If they invite us, we invite them,” he was quoted as saying by
Utusan Malaysia
today.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had earlier announced that the decision to invite PAS had been made in a consensus during a supreme council meeting.
Zahid said the Umno assembly this year would not decide on cooperation with any coalition, particularly ahead of the 16th general election.
He said discussions would instead focus on the potential benefits and risks to Umno and Barisan Nasional should any such cooperation be formed.
“Society wants Malays to champion Malay unity — not just within Umno, but across Malay parties.
“I don't want to unite Malay parties, but as a whole, Malays want Malay unity to be realised,” he was quoted as saying.

Title: Some Nepal villages so devastated, you’d think they never existed, says Malaysian relief volunteer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — Some villages in Nepal have been so completely devastated by the floods that there is no sign they ever existed, according to Malaysian relief volunteers who have seen the destruction first-hand.
Mercy Malaysia Rapid Assessment Team leader Vivegananthan Rajangam said some settlements along the rivers were left without a single house after the floods tore through Benighat, Nuwakot and Bidur.
“The damage is very severe. In some villages, there isn’t even one house left. If someone went there for the first time, they would think there was no village there,” he told
Harian Metro
today.
“In many places hit by the floods along the river, nobody lives there anymore. In some places, there is no trace of any houses at all.”
Even concrete buildings were not spared, with only about 20 per cent of such structures still standing in some settlements, he said.
“Most of these concrete buildings were also swept away,” Vivegananthan recounted.
Accumulated sludge lines the Trishuli riverbank after flash floods at Trishuli Bazar in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on September 5, 2026, as survivors struggle to rebuild homes destroyed by the disaster. — AFP pic
Survivors have since been moved away from the worst-hit areas, with many evacuated to Kathmandu and Nuwakot and housed in schools and halls on higher ground.
Vivegananthan said the Nepali authorities had also set up temporary shelters for those who survived the floods.
In Nuwakot alone, 19 such shelters have been established, he said.
Based on discussions with local authorities and assessments on the ground, food supplies at the shelters were adequate, but survivors needed other forms of assistance.
Mercy Malaysia’s three-member team will remain in Nepal for about 10 days to assess how best to support those who survived the disaster.
Mercy Malaysia’s Rapid Assessment Team assesses the extent of the flood devastation and health needs in Trishuli Dhunge Bazar, Bidur, as relief efforts continue in Nepal. — Picture from Facebook/MERCY Malaysia
Vivegananthan stressed that the team was not involved in search and rescue operations but was focused on helping survivors rebuild their lives.
“We are not involved in search and rescue. We are here to help those who survived,” he said.
Among the assistance provided are medicines, cooking equipment and toys for children, which are being channelled through Nepali authorities, including the country’s Health Ministry.
“The assistance we provide is aimed at helping them continue their lives as best as possible so they can return to normal,” Vivegananthan said.

Title: Two Fridays to go? Melaka CM Ab Rauf drops biggest hint yet on state assembly dissolution
Article:
MELAKA, Sept 7 — Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh today hinted that the state legislative assembly could be dissolved by the end of this month, paving the way for a state election.
The Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman said the dissolution would come in “two more Fridays”, suggesting an announcement could be made within the next two weeks, Harian Metro reported.
“Not long now. I said four Fridays the other day, but now there are only two Fridays left,” he was quoted saying during at a community programme in Sungai Udang here.
His remarks came a day after Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi urged Ab Rauf to speed up the dissolution announcement to allow the people, particularly young voters, to decide the state’s future.

Title: RM10,000 and a detour via Surabaya: Malaysian family stranded in Indonesia scrambles to get home after ash cloud cancels flights
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — A Malaysian family stranded in Jakarta after their flight home was cancelled has been forced to spend about RM10,000 on alternative travel, accommodation and transport to get back to Malaysia.
Wan Nor Ridani, 29, said his family had decided to travel by car to Surabaya before flying to Senai, Johor, as direct flights from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur were sold out,
Berita Harian
reported today.
“We have to think of other alternatives because the airport authorities cannot give any assurance when the situation will return to normal,” he was quoted as saying.
The family had already bought new tickets from Jakarta to Kuala Lumpur for tomorrow, but decided not to risk another cancellation as airport operations remained subject to intermittent closures.
Wan Nor Ridani said the airport’s operating suspension had been extended until 6pm today, leaving stranded passengers to make their own arrangements.
“Because of that, we will drive to Surabaya and from there take a flight to Senai. From Senai, we will continue to Kuala Lumpur because all direct flights to Kuala Lumpur are already sold out,” he said.
He said he had to split up from some family members as they were unable to secure flights from Surabaya and were still looking for other options.
The continuing eruption of Anak Krakatau since Friday has spread volcanic ash across the region, disrupting domestic and international flights and forcing several airports to suspend operations.
Wan Nor Ridani said the disruption had also sent hotel demand near the airport soaring, with many properties already full.
“Many people are stranded at the airport. Hotels around the airport are all full. The queues to reschedule flights are also very long. Some have been waiting since morning and only got their turn in the afternoon,” he added.

Title: Appeals court reserves decision on bid to stay committal proceedings against former undang Mubarak, five others
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — The Court of Appeal reserved its decision on an application by six individuals, including former Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Mubarak Thahak, to stay the committal proceedings against them pending disposal of their appeal.
A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Alwi Abdul Wahab, Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman and Datuk Amarjeet Singh set September 14 for case management to set the date for decision.
The court also extended the ad interim stay of the committal proceedings granted to the six individuals until a decision is made on their stay application.
A different three-man bench of the Court of Appeal had granted the ad interim stay on July 29 pending today’s hearing on the stay application.
Today, the bench heard full arguments for stay of committal proceedings from counsel Awang Armadajaya Awang Mahmud, who represented the applicants, and lawyer Steven Thiru, who appeared for the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang Negeri Sembilan (DKU) and its secretary, Raja Norazli Raja Nordin.
The six individuals comprising four Undangs and two chieftains have appealed against the decision of the Seremban High Court granting the DKU and Raja Norazli leave to commence committal proceedings against them for allegedly breaching an injunction order. Their appeal is scheduled for case management on Oct 19.
The six applicants are Mubarak, Undang Luak of Jelebu Datuk Maarof Mat Rashad, Undang Luak of Johol Datuk Muhammed Abdullah, Undang Luak of Rembau Datuk Abdul Rahim Yasin, Tunku Besar Tampin Tunku Syed Razman Tunku Syed Idrus Al-Qadri, and Shahbandar Sungai Ujong Datuk Seri Badarudin Abdul Khalid.
In his submissions, Awang Armadajaya said if the stay is not granted, it would render the applicants’ appeal nugatory.
He said there are important legal issues for determination of the Court of Appeal, including whether the High Court or the Special Court had the jurisdiction to hear the injunction and committal proceedings.
He said if the Court of Appeal decide that only the Special Court had jurisdiction, then the case must be brought before the Special Court for determination and all the proceedings in the High Court would be invalid.
Steven, meanwhile, urged the court to dismiss the stay application and allow the committal proceedings in the High Court to proceed without any delay.
He said established legal principle requires contempt proceedings, once commenced, to be given priority over other proceedings, adding that the applicants should instead seek an urgent hearing of their appeal.
Steven further argued that the applicants have shown disrespect to the court and have interfered with the administration of justice and they should not be granted any relief under Section 44 of the Courts of Judicature Act.
The legal dispute originated on May 5 this year when Mubarak and five others filed an originating summons at the High Court to obtain a copy of the minutes of a special DKU meeting held on April 17. Among the contents of the meeting minutes was a decision to remove Mubarak as Undang Luak of Sungai Ujong.
On June 5 this year, the High Court granted an ad interim injunction to preserve the status quo, maintaining the existing composition of the DKU and Raja Norazli’s position as its secretary, pending the determination of issues relating to jurisdiction and justiciability, or until further order of the court.
However, Raja Norazli claimed that media reports on the same day showed that the plaintiffs, particularly Maarof, had been involved in the purported appointment of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan under Article 11 of the Negeri Sembilan State Constitution 1959, despite the injunction order still being in force.
He alleged that the appointment was made in defiance of the court order, prompting the DKU and Raja Norazli to seek leave from the High Court to commence committal proceedings against the six individuals for contempt of court. — Bernama

Title: Police: Missing hikers said they were in good condition when speaking to family on Tuesday
Article:
GERIK, Sept 7 —Police said the six hikers, who are feared missing on Gunung Trans Gerah in Kelantan, were in good condition when they last contacted their family members on Tuesday (Sept 1), before continuing their journey towards Perak.
District police chief Supt Abdul Samad Othman said the group last contacted their family at 7.47 am that day.
“The group began their hike on Aug 29 from the Pos Dakoh area in Gua Musang, Kelantan, and were expected to make their way out via Pos Kemar, Perak on Sept 3.
“However, as of Sept 6 (yesterday), their family members had yet to hear from them and subsequently lodged a police report out of concern for their safety,” he said in a statement today.
He said following the report, the police, together with the relevant agencies, had coordinated a search and rescue (SAR) operation to locate the group along the trail on the Perak side.
It was reported earlier that the six individuals comprised Wan Ahmad Aslam Wan Zairudin, 39, Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, their children Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, and two mountain guides, Shafiee Sidek, 49, and Hazman Mamat, 43. — Bernama

Title: Police confirm RM27.5m drug syndicate crippled with main suspect shot dead
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police’s (PDRM) Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) crippled a drug processing syndicate suspected of producing Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) worth a total of RM27.5 million in this district and Kuala Lumpur in Op Thrips yesterday.
Bukit Aman NCID director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said in the raid, the 52-year-old main suspect was shot dead after he acted aggressively by firing shots at the raiding team at a terraced house in this district at about 1.30 pm.
He said the house rented by the suspect had been used as a laboratory to process the drugs since early this year, adding that police seized suspected MDMA comprising 64.49 kilogrammes (kg) of liquid, 5.2kg of drug lumps, 7.9kg of drug pills, 104.8kg of drug powder, as well as various drug-processing equipment.
“We believe the suspect obtained the drugs with the assistance of other syndicate members by bringing in drug-processing precursors from abroad.
“The suspect who was shot dead also had the expertise to process these chemicals into MDMA or ecstasy,” he said at a press conference at the Seremban district police headquarters (IPD) here today.
It was believed that the suspect had extensive experience, as his involvement in drug-related activities had been detected since the 1990s, in addition to having three previous arrest and imprisonment records under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Hussein said the main suspect was also wanted under Section 3(1) of the Kidnapping Act 1961, in addition to having a previous criminal record under Section 448 of the Penal Code.
He added that the syndicate’s modus operandi was to use residential areas with low population density as locations for processing and distributing drugs to conceal their activities from the authorities.
Hussein said the drugs were believed to be intended for the local and overseas markets, while police were now actively tracking down several more suspects believed to have fled abroad.
Meanwhile, he said police also conducted two separate raids in Seremban 2 and at a house in Kuchai Lama, Kuala Lumpur, which led to the arrest of a 32-year-old woman and a 35-year-old man.
Both the woman and man tested positive for methamphetamine and THC, respectively, and both had various previous criminal records, including drug-related offences. They were remanded for seven days until Sept 13.
Hussein said police also seized three cars and that the case was being investigated under Section 307 of the Penal Code and Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
He said the seizure could indirectly curb the distribution of drugs to more than 400,000 users. — Bernama

Title: Missing hiking family in Kelantan mountains never stayed out more than a day, says grandpa — now it’s been four, maybe without food
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The silence from his son’s family has left Wan Zairudin Wan Ismail fearing that something may have gone wrong during their hike through the Kelantan forest.
His son Wan Ahmad Aslam, 39, daughter-in-law Siti Zulaiha Norizan, 39, grandchildren Diya Raisha, 13, and Ahmad Raef, 9, and their two mountain guides have been missing since failing to emerge from the forest as scheduled last Thursday.
“I am worried that someone may have been injured,” Wan Zairudin, 66, who lives in Shah Alam, Selangor, was quoted by
The New Straits Times
as saying today.
The family was last heard from on September 1, when Siti Zulaiha messaged her mother-in-law to say they were safe and expected to reach Pos Kemar in Perak two days later.
Wan Zairudin is also concerned that the group may be running out of food, as their supplies were expected to last only six or seven days.
The six were reported missing after they failed to return as scheduled and repeated attempts to contact them were unsuccessful.
Wan Zairudin lodged a police report at the Bukit Jelutong police station in Shah Alam two days ago.
The Fire and Rescue Department launched a search and rescue operation today, including a helicopter-assisted search to locate the group and trace the route they were believed to have taken.
“My son is a project manager in Yong Peng, Johor, while my daughter-in-law works in Simpang Renggam. They often go hiking with their two children, and the longest they had ever stayed in the forest beyond their scheduled exit was just one day,” he said.
“This time, however, it is worrying as they have now gone four days without sufficient food.”
Wan Zairudin said he had sent the family to Terminal Bersepadu Selatan in Cheras on Aug 29 to catch a bus to Gua Musang, while their car was left at his home in Shah Alam.
The family was due to return by bus from either Gerik or Kuala Kangsar last Thursday before travelling back to Yong Peng, with the children expected to return to school after the holidays ended yesterday.
Wan Zairudin said his son had chosen the Trans GBB route, which he had never attempted before, as part of his plan to complete several mountain expeditions in Malaysia before taking his family to climb Mount Kinabalu next year.
“I am worried that someone may have been injured, perhaps suffering a sprained ankle and being unable to move. Without outside help, it would be difficult for them to get out of the forest,” he said.
Wan Zairudin said the family knew Trans GBB was among the more challenging hiking routes.
He and his wife planned to travel to Gerik today, where search and rescueoperations room had been set up, to seek the latest updates on their family.

Title: Shahrir Samad and Tommy Thomas discussing possible resolution of civil suit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The High Court today adjourned proceedings in the civil suit filed by Tan Sri Shahrir Samad against former Attorney General Tan Sri Tommy Thomas, former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Latheefa Koya, and two others, to facilitate settlement negotiations among the parties.
Judge Gan Techiong ordered the adjournment after Shahrir’s counsel Datuk Firoz Hussein Ahmad Jamaluddin informed the court that his client and the defendants were discussing a possible resolution of the matter.
“As we have indicated earlier, there have been some positive developments and discussions between the plaintiff and the second to fourth defendants. In that regard, we need to obtain further instructions from our client,” said Firoz Hussein.
“We seek Your Lordship’s leave and permission to discuss the matter, specifically the proposed resolution of the dispute. We also respectfully request that this morning’s proceedings be vacated to enable us to continue those discussions. We will return before Your Lordship on Wednesday (Sept 9),” he added.
Counsel Alan Adrian Gomez, representing Thomas as the first defendant, and senior federal counsel Zureen Elina Mohd Dom, appearing for the three other defendants, confirmed that the parties were engaged in settlement discussions and raised no objection to adjourning today’s proceedings.
Judge Gan then adjourned the proceedings to Sept 9 for the parties to update the court on the status of the proposed settlement.
Shahrir had been scheduled to continue giving his testimony in the matter today.
In December 2023, Shahrir filed the civil suit against Thomas, Latheefa, the MACC, and the Government of Malaysia, alleging malicious prosecution.
The former Johor Bahru Member of Parliament’s claim arises from a RM1 million cheque he had received from former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak for rehabilitation works on the Puri Langkasuka housing project in Larkin, Johor.
Thomas, who served as Attorney General from June 2018 to February 2020, has denied Shahrir’s allegations against him, including abuse of power, describing them as “indefensible.”
He further clarified that he had resigned on Feb 28, 2020, and that Shahrir’s criminal trial commenced only on July 26, 2022.
On Jan 5, 2023, High Court Judge Datuk Muhammad Jamil Hussin acquitted Shahrir of the charge of failing to declare to the Inland Revenue Board the RM1 million in income received from Najib. — Bernama

Title: Hadi ready to face police over US ‘topple govt’ claim, says aide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang is expected to give a statement to police after Bukit Aman contacted him over his claim that the United States sought to help topple the Malaysian government before the 2018 general election.
Hadi’s political secretary Syahir Sulaiman said the PAS president was ready to cooperate, although no date has been fixed for his statement, Berita Harian reported today.
“Yes, Bukit Aman has contacted us. Hadi has been informed and is ready to give the police his full cooperation,” Syahir was quoted as saying.
Three police reports have been lodged over Hadi’s claim that the US offered assistance to topple the government in 2014.
He made the allegation at the 72nd PAS congress in Kelantan, claiming several PAS leaders had been invited to meet US Embassy representatives during then-president Barack Obama’s visit to Malaysia that year.
The US Embassy in Kuala Lumpur has denied the allegation, saying its representatives had never offered to help PAS oust the then-Barisan Nasional government.
Chargé d’affaires ad interim David H. Gamble Jr said the United States had never sought to determine Malaysia’s political leadership.

Title: No new wage target, but economy minister says govt wants greater transparency in salary offers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Economy Ministry is looking at ways to make salary offers more transparent and equitable, rather than setting an absolute wage target.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said wage growth was important to ensure the benefits of economic growth were felt by the people.
“Median wages are around RM3,600, but there is still a gap, particularly among the Bumiputera,” he told reporters after a dialogue session at the Royale Chulan hotel here.
Akmal said greater transparency was needed in salary offers to ensure workers received fairer returns for their contributions.
“We need greater transparency in wages, and there should be a mandate for salary offers to be made more transparent and fair,” he said, adding that he would bring the matter back to the Economy Ministry for further consideration.
He said equal opportunities for workers could also be reassessed to ensure young people and other workers had better opportunities and received wages commensurate with their contributions.
Akmal stressed that the approach was not about setting a single absolute salary figure, but about ensuring greater openness and fairness in the wages being offered.
He said wages should, as far as possible, meet people’s expenditure needs, with the Perceived Adequacy of Household Expenditure indicator taking into account factors such as location and household size.
“In the context of wages, what we are looking at is greater transparency in salary offers, rather than setting an absolute figure,” he said.

Title: Four days overdue, rescuers mount land, air and water search for six hikers in Kelantan mountains
Article:
GERIK, Sept 7 — Rescue teams are being mobilised by water, land and air in preparation for a search and rescue (SAR) operation for six individuals feared missing while hiking at Gunung Trans Gerah in Lojing, Kelantan.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department (better known by its Malay initials JBPM) director Datuk Sayani Saidon said the department received information about the missing two mountain guides and four family members yesterday afternoon, prompting discussions with the JBPM
headquarters’ operations division on the search plan.
He said three boats from the Trojan Jetty in Gerik would transport eight members of the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Team and five fire and rescue mountain guides by water to Pos Kemar.
“A total of 12 Forestry Mountain Guides are also travelling from Sungai Siput in four-wheel-drive vehicles to Pos Kemar, with the journey expected to take about four hours.
“All teams will gather at Pos Kemar, which will serve as the Forward Control Post,” he said when contacted today.
Sayani said the JBPM air unit from the Northern Region JBPM Bertam Air Base was scheduled to depart Bertam at 2pm today for an aerial survey, beginning at the last location where the six were seen on Sept 1 before proceeding towards Pos Kemar.
“The aerial survey is important to give us an initial overview of the search area, including identifying routes that can be used by the ground teams,” he said.
He said the JBPM canine unit which arrived this morning, was on standby but had yet to be deployed pending finalisation of the operation plan.
“A multi-agency coordination meeting is still being held at the Gerik District Police Headquarters to determine the SAR plan and deployment on the ground,” he said.
The operation involves the Royal Malaysia Police, Forestry Department, Department of Wildlife and National Parks, General Operations Force, JBPM and Forestry Mountain Guides.
The six began their hike on Aug 29 and were due to emerge from the forest on Sept 3.
A report was lodged by their family members yesterday after they failed to return as scheduled. — Bernama

Title: Ex-Felda general manager under five-day remand as MACC digs into KL land deal
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 7 — A former Felda general manager has been remanded for five days to assist investigations into an abuse of power case involving the appointment of a developer for a project in Kuala Lumpur and the sale of land owned by the statutory body.
The remand order, which runs from today until Sept 11, was issued by Magistrate Ezrene Zakariah after the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) made the application at the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court here.
The suspect, who is in his late 60s, was among two men in their 50s and 60s called by MACC to assist in the investigation.
Both are suspected of being involved in the sale of the statutory body’s land to a company with interests in the developer, without the knowledge of its board of directors and subsidiary.
It was reported that MACC detained two individuals, including a former general manager of a statutory body with the title ‘Datuk’, at about 4pm yesterday after they appeared at the MACC headquarters here to have their statements recorded.
Yesterday, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests and said the case was being investigated under Section 16 of the MACC Act 2009.
Last week, MACC opened seven investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).
Abd Halim was reported as saying that the large-scale special investigation, ‘Ops Fella’, focuses on investment transactions and asset acquisitions by Felda and FIC management between 2010 and 2020.
Six of the seven investigation papers were opened on Aug 24, while the remaining one is an old case that is still active and undergoing the Mutual Legal Assistance (MLA) process.
The investigations cover the investment in Syarikat Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd, based in Limbang, Sarawak, the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah and the purchase of Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments in London.
They also cover the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd, the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House, and alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.
The old investigation involving the Park City Grand Plaza property, which is still active and undergoing the MLA process, is also being reviewed in parallel, bringing the total number of cases under the seven investigation papers.
Meanwhile, a source said a remand application for the other individual, who is currently receiving treatment for what is believed to be health problems, would be made at a hospital today. — Bernama

Title: Anthony Loke: Steps taken to strengthen checks on aviation personnel including pilots and cabin crew
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 7 — The Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) are taking steps to strengthen checks on pilots, cabin crew and other aviation personnel following the case involving a Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilot linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said that was the least they could do now, as the MOT was not privy to details of the police investigation, including the identities of suspects or any arrests made, as the matter was being investigated as a criminal case.
“I’m still not privy to the details…We have read that several arrests have been made, so it is better for the police to be the one making further announcements on the matter,” he said when asked at a press conference held in conjunction with the 61st Directors General of Civil Aviation Conference for the Asia-Pacific Region (DGCA/61) here today.
Loke said MOT would definitely provide full cooperation to police, including access to airport facilities and any information or personnel required for the investigation.
“The investigation is under the police. They have no obligation to inform us or to discuss with us the progress of the investigation, but we will give our cooperation by providing whatever information or access is needed, whether to our facilities or airports, as well as any personnel they want to interview or investigate,” he said.
Last Sept 4, Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police have arrested six local men suspected of involvement in an international drug trafficking syndicate linked to the arrest of a Malaysian co-pilot in Jakarta last July.
The arrests followed information obtained from the 39-year-old co-pilot during questioning by an NCID team sent to Jakarta from Aug 11 to 15.
Media reports previously stated that the co-pilot was arrested at Terminal 3 of Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on suspicion of attempting to smuggle 25 kilogrammes of drugs and that the Indonesian National Police (POLRI) reportedly seized 15 packages containing 70,114 ecstasy pills and methamphetamine, with an estimated value of RM45 million.
Meanwhile, on flight diversions following the volcanic ash in Jakarta, CAAM chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said Malaysia was assisting by serving as an alternate airport for flights originally bound for Jakarta.
“For Malaysia, we assist them as an alternate airport. So, some aircraft inbound to Jakarta are being diverted to KLIA, so we are supporting them in that respect,” he said.  — Bernama

Title: Two women remanded over alleged child mistreatment at Pahang nurseries
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 7 — Two women have been remanded for six days to assist in investigations into the alleged mistreatment of children at childcare centres in Kuantan and Temerloh.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the two nursery staff, aged 31 and 26, were remanded for six days until Saturday (Sept 12) following applications by police at the Kuantan and Temerloh Magistrates’ Courts.
He said the 31-year-old woman was detained yesterday to assist in investigations into the alleged mistreatment of a two-year-old boy at a nursery in Bukit Setongkol here.
“Another woman was detained to facilitate investigations into allegations of mistreatment involving a two-year-old girl at a nursery in Temerloh,” he said in a statement today.
Kuantan district police chief ACP Ashari Abu Samah said yesterday that police received a report concerning a viral video showing a toddler being scolded, having his hair pulled and his head shaken by a woman working at the centre.
Meanwhile, Temerloh district police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said police received a report from the child’s 29-year-old mother at about 6 pm yesterday over allegations that her two-year-old daughter had been mistreated by a nanny at a nursery near Temerloh.
The video showing the alleged mistreatment of the child by the nursery caretaker has also gone viral on social media, drawing widespread public attention. — Bernama

Title: Communications minister: Nadi-PKD synergy to optimise government resources, boost public service delivery
Article:
CYBERJAYA, Sept 7 — Efforts to strengthen collaboration between the National Information Dissemination Centres (Nadi) and Rural Community Centres (PKD) under the Rural and Regional Development Ministry (KKDW) reflect the government’s focus on synergy, resource optimisation and better public service delivery.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Nadi had evolved beyond providing computers and Internet access to become community information and empowerment hubs connecting people with skills, opportunities and government services.
“There are 191 PKDs under KKDW, equipped with facilities, resources and community networks. Given the strengths of both PKD and Nadi, I believe there is significant scope for them to complement each other and strengthen service delivery to the people.
“This is the whole-of-government approach we need to put into practice. It is not about who owns a facility, but how existing government facilities and resources can be fully utilised for the benefit of the people,” he said at the PKD-NADI Strategic Collaboration Workshop here today.
Also present were Deputy Prime Minister and Rural and Regional Development Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) chairman Tan Sri Mohamad Salim Fateh Din.
Fahmi said the approach was in line with the government’s efforts to promote a cashless society, including the use of e-wallets, while digital empowerment should now be expanded to include artificial intelligence (AI) skills.
“Our hope is for each Nadi to produce at least one prompt engineer. If we prepare young people for the future by teaching them to harness cloud technology and AI, they can develop applications that benefit their communities and local economies,” he said.
In a separate development, Fahmi said he had instructed MCMC to take firm action against the misuse of e-commerce platforms or online marketplaces to sell drugs, including fentanyl.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had also contacted him about the issue, which was becoming increasingly concerning.
“I have instructed MCMC, and they will be meeting one of the platforms that we believe has been involved in the misuse of networks enabling drugs such as fentanyl, or what is known as ‘piu-piu’, to be sold in Malaysia,” he said.
Fahmi said government efforts to provide reliable Internet access and improve PKD and Nadi facilities were aimed at narrowing the digital divide between rural, suburban and urban communities.
“But if these communications networks are not secure and users lack the knowledge or skills to protect themselves, it will not only enable drugs to be sold more widely, but also give rise to other problems, including scams,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Inquest told father never consulted over Zara’s autopsy
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 7 — The Coroner’s Court heard today that the father of the late Zara Qairina Mahathir was never asked for his consent regarding an autopsy on his daughter.
Testifying before Coroner Amir Shah Amir Hassan, Mahathir Mohd Hashim @ Marikin, 45, said a doctor confirmed Zara's death in his presence at Queen Elizabeth Hospital I (HQE I) on July 17, 2025.
The 80th witness stated he stayed overnight at the hospital after arriving at the emergency unit on the afternoon of July 16 upon learning of her admission.
Mahathir told the court that a attending female doctor informed him Zara was in critical condition with a broken leg and severe internal bleeding in her brain, lungs, and kidneys, adding that she would remain permanently comatose if she survived.
He further testified that he observed blood on his daughter's pillow, felt an apparent depression at the soft upper back of her neck when kissing her forehead, and noted her left leg was bandaged from thigh to sole. — Daily Express
